title: Bloom filter probe: hash+lookup only run heads of equal consecutive keys
hypothesis: Warm profile of q21 (3rd run in the same process, JSON profiling): the l2 and l3 lineitem scans carry `optional: l_orderkey IN BF(l_orderkey)` and cost 0.72s and 0.86s CPU for 60M rows each. A plain warm 2-column scan of the same columns costs 0.18s CPU, and hashing 60M BIGINTs costs about 0.15s (EXPLAIN ANALYZE bit_xor(hash(l_orderkey))). So about 0.4-0.5s per scan is hashing plus random BF lookups: 708K keys give a 2MB filter, which misses L2. That is about 1.2s of the query's ~4.7s CPU. lineitem is clustered on the join key (about 4 consecutive rows per key), so most hash/lookup work repeats the previous row's. If BFTableFilter::Filter checks whether key[i]==key[i-1] and reuses the previous result, hashing and lookups drop about 4x on clustered data.
plan: In src/planner/filter/bloom_filter.cpp, BFTableFilter::Filter: add a fast path when keys_v is a FLAT_VECTOR, its physical type is a fixed-width integer (INT8..INT64, UINT8..UINT64; a template over T), and it has no NULLs in the approved rows (validity AllValid, or a cheap per-row check). Steps: (1) walk the approved rows (through sel if set, otherwise 0..count-1) and write the positions where key != previous approved key into a head selection (state.bf_sel or a new buffer in BFTableFilterState, src/include/duckdb/planner/table_filter_state.hpp). (2) If heads > ~3/4 of approved_tuple_count, fall back to the existing path, so unclustered data pays only one compare per row. (3) Otherwise slice keys_v by the head sel, run VectorOperations::Hash on the heads only, and call filter.LookupOne per head (or LookupHashes). (4) Walk the approved rows again, carrying the current head's found flag, and compact sel / approved_tuple_count the way the current code does (keep the existing semantics: sel.Initialize(bf_sel) when sel was not set, otherwise remap). Results are identical to the per-row path because equal keys hash identically. Do not touch BloomFilter itself.
expected_gain: q21: l2+l3 scans 1.58s → ~0.8s CPU, out of ~4.7s total CPU. Roughly -8..-15% wall. Also l1-type scans if a BF is ever pushed on a clustered key.
generality: Helps any join-filter BF probe on a column stored clustered or sorted by the join key, which is common for fact tables loaded in key order (lineitem/orders, events by id, time-sorted data): semi joins, delim joins, FK joins with selective build sides. Unclustered columns pay one extra compare per row plus the fallback check, under 0.5ns/row.
risk: Low. Results are unchanged by construction. The main correctness hazards are NULL handling (fall back when any NULL is present) and sel remapping. Edge risk: the adaptive fallback threshold is wrong for data that alternates between clustered and not, costing a small amount of extra work.
